questions.q: Match complication timing per the book's flowchart — 1) Operative 2) Acute post operative 3) Late post operative … A) PCO, phimosis, Irvin-Gass B) PCR, UGH, expulsive haemorrhage, Descemet detachment C) Endophthalmitis, iris prolapse, flat AC
questions.exp: Complications: Operative, Acute post operative, Late post operative. (Book p83)

questions.q: Causes of posterior capsular rupture per the book are:
opts: Incomplete hydrodissection: capsule aspirated along with cortex, defective nuclear fragmentation
questions.exp: Causes: D/t incomplete hydrodissection: Capsule aspirated along with cortex; Defective nuclear fragmentation. (Book p83)

questions.q: Fill up: Complications of PCR include implantation disturbance and fall of IOL into the ___, resolved by implantation at sulcus or anterior chamber.
questions.exp: Complications of PCR: Implantation disturbance, Fall of IOL into the vitreous Resolved by implantation at Sulcus, Anterior chamber, Vitreous in anterior segment. (Book p83)

questions.q: UGH syndrome per the book is:
opts: Uveitis - Glaucoma - Hyphema (Collection of blood in AC)
questions.exp: UGH SYNDROME Uveitis - Glaucoma - Hyphema (Collection of blood in AC). (Book p83)

questions.q: Fill up: Cause of UGH per the book is ACIOL implantation → ___ chafing.
questions.exp: Causes: ACIOL implantation → Iris chafing. (Book p83)

questions.q: Match ACIOL iris chafing consequence per the book — 1) Inflammation 2) Glaucoma 3) Hyphema … A) Pigment blocking trabecular meshwork (Iris pigmented tissue) B) Uveitis C) D/t vascularity of iris
questions.exp: Complications specific to ACIOL Iris chafing → Inflammation uveitis, Glaucoma pigment blocking trabecular meshwork (Iris pigmented tissue), Hyphema D/t vascularity of iris. (Book p83)

questions.q: Management of UGH per the book and prognosis:
opts: Steroids + anti-glaucoma agents, explant ACIOL if severe, slower recovery 7-10 days vs 24h normal
Topical antibiotics + systemic steroids, retain ACIOL always, rapid recovery 24-48h regain vision
Immediate evisceration with scleral implant, no steroids, permanent vision loss expected
Observation only, no medical therapy, spontaneous resolution within 2-3 days without intervention
questions.exp: Management: Steroids/antiglaucoma agents, Explant ACIOL (in severe cases), Slower prognosis: 7-10 days to regain vision (24 hours normally). (Book p83)

questions.q: Expulsive choroidal haemorrhage cause per the book:
opts: Pressure difference during surgery → haemorrhage of choroidal vessels, short posterior ciliary artery
Trauma to inner surface cornea by instrument
questions.exp: Cause: Pressure difference during surgery → Haemorrhage of choroidal vessels Short posterior ciliary artery. (Book p84)

questions.q: Match short posterior ciliary artery supply per the book — 1) Posterior sclera/choroid 2) Outer 4 layers retina … A) Supplies posterior portion of sclera, choroid B) Supplies outer 4 layers of retina C) Supplies inner retina
questions.exp: Short posterior ciliary artery Supplies Posterior portion sclera choroid Outer 4 layers retina. (Book p84)

questions.q: Fill up: Descemet membrane detachment cause is trauma to the inner surface of cornea d/t entry/exit of instrument during surgeries, treatment is descemetopexy → air bubble in ___.
questions.exp: Cause: Trauma to inner surface cornea d/t entry/exit instrument; Treatment: Descemetopexy → Air bubble in anterior chamber. (Book p84)

questions.q: Iris prolapse acute post operative complication is due to:
opts: Defective closure of incision in periphery of cornea
questions.exp: Iris prolapse: D/t defective closure of incision in the periphery of cornea. (Book p84)

questions.q: Which statement about endophthalmitis is TRUE per the book?
opts: Suppurative inflammation all layers except sclera, etiology infective per book
Suppurative inflammation only cornea and conjunctiva, etiology allergic per book
Non-infective granulomatous inflammation of sclera only, etiology autoimmune
Suppurative inflammation includes sclera always, etiology purely traumatic non-infective
questions.exp: Endophthalmitis (EO): Suppurative inflammation of all layers of eyeball except sclera; Etiology: Infective. (Book p84)

questions.q: Match agent with m/c cause of endophthalmitis per p84 table — 1) Staph epidermidis/Coag neg staph 2) Propionibacterium acnes 3) Bacillus cereus 4) Klebsiella 5) Candida … A) Acute onset <7 days post-op EO B) Late onset 6 weeks-6 months post-op EO C) Post traumatic EO D) Bacterial endogenous EO E) Fungal endogenous EO
questions.exp: Table: Staph epidermidis/Coag neg staph Acute onset <7 days Post-op EO, Propionibacterium acnes Late onset 6w-6mo Post-op EO, Bacillus cereus Post traumatic EO, Klebsiella Bacterial endogenous EO, Candida Fungal endogenous EO. (Book p84)

questions.q: All are symptoms of endophthalmitis per p85 EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Symptoms: Pain, Redness, Loss of vision. (Book p85)

questions.q: Fill up: Sign of endophthalmitis in anterior chamber is hypopyon/pus, with hazy cornea, congestion/hyperemia, posterior segment yellowish exudates in ___.
questions.exp: Signs: Anterior chamber Hypopyon/pus Hazy cornea Congestion/hyperemia Posterior segment Yellowish exudates in vitreous. (Book p85)

questions.q: Management per assessment of vision in endophthalmitis per the book — Clinical blindness No PL vs Visual potential present:
opts: No PL → evisceration (all except sclera); Visual potential → pars plana vitrectomy + intravitreal vancomycin 1mg/0.1mL + ceftazidime 2.2mg/0.1mL + topical antibiotics
No PL → topical antibiotics only and observation; Visual potential → systemic steroids only, no vitrectomy
Visual potential → immediate evisceration; No PL → intravitreal antibiotics only, no surgery needed
Both groups → systemic antibiotics only, no intravitreal or vitrectomy, conservative management
questions.exp: Assessment: Clinical blindness No perception of light: Surgical removal Evisceration Removal all layers except sclera; Visual potential present Posterior segment coverage + Anterior segment coverage Pars plana vitrectomy Intravitreal antibiotics Vancomycin 1mg in 0.1mL Ceftazidime 2.2mg in 0.1mL Topical antibiotics. (Book p85)

questions.q: Which statement about endophthalmitis antibiotics is TRUE per p85 note?
opts: Systemic antibiotics have major role in healing endophthalmitis
Systemic antibiotics have no role in healing endophthalmitis; intravitreal Vancomycin 1mg/0.1mL and Ceftazidime 2.2mg/0.1mL used
questions.exp: Note: Systemic antibiotics have no role in healing endophthalmitis. Intravitreal Vancomycin 1mg in 0.1mL Ceftazidime 2.2mg in 0.1mL. (Book p85)

questions.q: All are causes of flat/shallow AC per the book EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Flat/shallow AC: Wound leak, Malignant glaucoma, Pupillary block glaucoma, Cilio-choroidal detachment. Other complications: Uveitis, Retinal detachment, Astigmatism. PCO is late. (Book p85)

questions.q: Other complications listed besides flat AC per p85 are:
questions.exp: Other complications: Uveitis, Retinal detachment, Astigmatism. (Book p85)

questions.q: Posterior capsular opacification per the book:
opts: AKA 2° cataract, m/c late 6-12w, painless gradual vision loss, square edged IOL reduces occurrence
Acute complication <7 days post-op, painful red eye, treated with intravitreal antibiotics
Due to bacterial infection of vitreous, presents with hypopyon and requires evisceration
Treated with topical steroids only, no YAG needed, resolves spontaneously in 2-3 weeks
questions.exp: PCO AKA 2° cataract after cataract m/c late complication 6-12 weeks Causes gradual painless loss vision Square edged IOL reduce occurrence Pathology Posterior collection residual epithelial cells. (Book p86)

questions.q: Match PCO pathology per p86 — 1) Soemmerring's ring 10% 2) Elschnig's pearls 90% 3) Capsular wrinkling … A) Residual epithelial cells collection posterior B) Specific % noted C) Wrinkling of capsule
questions.exp: Pathology Posterior collection residual epithelial cells Soemmerring's ring 10% Elschnig's pearls 90% Capsular wrinkling. (Book p86)

questions.q: Fill up: Treatment of PCO is Nd:YAG laser posterior capsulotomy, mechanism ___.
questions.exp: Treatment: Nd:YAG laser posterior capsulotomy Mechanism Photodisruption. (Book p86)

questions.q: A patient 2 months after cataract surgery shows contraction of anterior capsule due to fibrosis leading to IOL decentration, image shows AC phimosis. Per the book this is:
questions.exp: ANTERIOR CAPSULE PHIMOSIS Contraction anterior capsule d/t fibrosis → IOL decentration image AC phimosis. (Book p86)

questions.q: Match Irvin-Gass syndrome triad per p86 — occurs 6 to 10 weeks after Sx — 1) CME 2) Bullous keratopathy 3) Vitreous wick … A) Cystoid macular edema B) Bullous keratopathy C) Vitreous strand touching cornea
questions.exp: IRVIN GLASS SYNDROME Occurs 6 to 10 weeks after Sx Triad Cystoid macular edema CME Bullous Keratopathy Vitreous strand touching cornea vitreous wick. (Book p86)

questions.q: Match IOL dislocation direction with syndrome per the book — 1) Upwards 2) Downwards 3) Lost lens … A) Sunrise syndrome B) Sunset syndrome C) IOL falls into vitreous D/t PCR or spontaneous Hallerman-Streiff
questions.exp: IOL DISLOCATION Upwards Sunrise syndrome Downwards Sunset syndrome Lost lens syndrome IOL falls into vitreous D/t PCR Spontaneous Hallerman-Streiff syndrome. (Book p86)

questions.q: All are causes of IOL dislocation/lost lens syndrome per the book EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Lost lens syndrome IOL falls into vitreous D/t PCR Spontaneous Hallerman-Streiff syndrome. (Book p86)
